title: The Quiet Floor

lines: 21:42, Zone 4 AutoStore grid. Three failed retrieval attempts in six minutes — no hard fault code, no stoppage.
Every customer-facing dashboard still reads green. A change log shows a firmware push to that zone two hours earlier, ahead of peak-season load testing.
Nothing here is on fire. But something changed, and the floor hasn't fully settled since.

drills.description_seed: Zone 4 showing intermittent retry faults following an unconfirmed firmware push, three days ahead of peak trading.

concept: A Major Incident doesn't wait for visible damage. The real test: does it need another team, could it reach a customer, has it gone unresolved a while — Zone 4 already met one of the three, quiet or not.

title: Every Light at Once

lines: 21:45, Zones 2 and 3. Every unit alarms within the same ninety seconds — the floor display is a wall of red.
Two floor staff are already at the panel. It looks like the biggest thing that's happened all week.
Nobody's checked the maintenance calendar yet.

drills.title: Zones 2/3 simultaneous fault alerts
drills.description_seed: Simultaneous fault alerts across Zones 2 and 3, cross-checking against the maintenance calendar.

concept: Priority runs on Impact × Urgency, not decibels. A wall of red lights that clears itself on schedule carries a different Priority than one unit quietly failing near a deadline — same matrix, very different inputs.

title: One Aisle, Not Everyone

lines: 22:10, Packing Zone 6. The conveyor gate has jammed twice in ten minutes — the floor engineer is already elbow-deep in it.
Nothing's reached the website. Nothing's reached Despatch. But three totes are backing up behind the gate, and the engineer can't watch the queue and fix the gate at the same time.
Somebody outside this aisle needs to know what's happening before the queue gets any longer.

drills.title: Packing Zone 6 conveyor gate jam
drills.description_seed: Conveyor gate at Packing Zone 6 jamming repeatedly while the floor engineer works the fault; queue building behind it.

concept: Escalating isn't about noise — it's about routing. The engineer in the aisle didn't need paging; the team who could clear the backing queue did. Notify is how you get the right people moving without waking up everyone else.

title: On the Record

lines: 23:05, Pick-face Aisle 12. A handheld scanner started throwing read errors twenty minutes ago — enough to slow two pickers down.
A technician already swapped the unit. The aisle's moving again, no alarms, nothing outstanding.
The only thing left is making sure what actually happened tonight is on the record — not just talked about.

drills.title: Aisle 12 handheld scanner swap
drills.description_seed: Handheld scanner in Aisle 12 throwing read errors; unit swapped by floor technician.
drills.worklog_seed: Swapped faulty handheld scanner unit in Aisle 12. Confirmed clean reads on five consecutive scans before leaving the aisle.

concept: A WorkLog is your own time-tracked record of what you did — separate from a Note, which is just conversation with the requester or another technician. If it's not in a WorkLog, the ticket's history doesn't show it happened.

title: Closing It Right

lines: 04:10, Zone 4. WMS Engineering paused the firmware rollout platform-wide four hours ago, right after it reached Zone 5.
Both zones have been clean since. Every dashboard reads green, and the next shift is already filing in.
The ticket's still open. Closing it is the last thing standing between tonight and the handover.

drills.title: Zone 4/5 firmware rollout — retry fault
drills.description_seed: Firmware push caused intermittent retry faults in Zone 4, later reaching Zone 5. WMS Engineering paused the rollout platform-wide.
drills.closure_comment_seed: Firmware rollout paused platform-wide before further spread. Both zones clean since 00:10. Closing ahead of handover.

concept: Closure codes aren't just "Resolved." Resolved — Fixed, No Fault Found, Duplicate, and Cancelled all close a ticket, but they mean very different things in next month's report. Picking the right one is how "resolved" stays a useful word instead of a rubber stamp.
